table.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top used for eating meals.

chair.definition: A single seat with a back and four legs, for one person.

booth.definition: A table (in a restaurant or bar) surrounded by two high-backed benches.

menu.definition: A list of the food and drinks available to order.

napkin.definition: A small piece of table linen that is used to wipe the mouth and to cover the lap in order to protect clothing.

tablecloth.definition: A piece of cloth spread over a table for decoration or protection.

candle.definition: A wax cylinder with a wick that gives light when it burns.

centerpiece.definition: A decorative arrangement placed in the middle of a dining table.

place-setting.definition: The collection of dishes, eating utensils, drinkware, and a napkin arranged for one diner at a meal.

salt-shaker.definition: A small container with holes in its lid lets you sprinkle salt over food.

pepper-shaker.definition: A small container with a hole-covered lid is used to scatter ground pepper over food.

high-chair.definition: A tall chair with safety features designed for a small child to sit at table height.
high-chair.exampleUsage: The restaurant provided a high chair for the toddler.

bar-stool.definition: A tall seat designed for use at a high counter.
bar-stool.exampleUsage: The counter has several bar stools.

counter.definition: Table consisting of a horizontal surface over which business is transacted.

plate.definition: A flat round item used for serving a meal.

bowl.definition: A deep round item used for serving soup, cereal, or salad.

glass.definition: A clear drinking vessel without a handle.

fork.definition: A handheld eating tool with several narrow pointed teeth.
fork.exampleUsage: The fork was used during the activity.

knife.definition: A handheld tool with a sharp blade used for slicing ingredients.
knife.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "knife" in an educational description.

spoon.definition: A handheld eating tool with a small rounded end for liquids or soft meals.
spoon.exampleUsage: The spoon was used during the activity.

cup.definition: A small drinking vessel, usually with a handle.

saucer.definition: A small shallow item placed beneath a drinking vessel.

mug.definition: A sturdy drinking vessel with a handle, often used for hot drinks.

chopsticks.definition: A pair of thin sticks held in one hand to pick up food.

straw.definition: A narrow tube used to drink liquid.

serving-tray.definition: A flat portable surface used to carry food, dishes, or drinks.
serving-tray.exampleUsage: The server carried the plates on a serving tray.

pitcher.definition: A large vessel with a handle and spout for serving drinks.

wine-glass.definition: A stemmed drinking glass traditionally used for wine.
wine-glass.exampleUsage: The table-setting display included an empty wine glass.

waiter.definition: A person whose occupation is to serve at table (as in a restaurant).

waitress.definition: A woman whose job is to serve customers at restaurant tables.

chef.definition: A professional cook, especially one in charge of a kitchen.

cook.definition: A person whose job is to prepare food.

host.definition: A restaurant worker who welcomes guests and arranges their seating.

hostess.definition: A woman who greets guests and helps seat them at a restaurant.

busser.definition: A restaurant worker clears used dishes, wipes and resets tables, and helps waiters serve diners.

bartender.definition: An employee who mixes and serves alcoholic drinks at a bar.

dishwasher.definition: A kitchen worker who washes dishes and utensils.
dishwasher.exampleUsage: The dishwasher washes the plates after dinner.

manager.definition: A person who controls resources and expenditures.

sommelier.definition: A waiter who manages wine service in a hotel or restaurant.

barista.definition: A coffee shop worker who prepares and serves coffee drinks.

appetizer.definition: Food or drink to stimulate the appetite (usually served before a meal or as the first course).

main-course.definition: The principal dish in a formal meal is served as the meal’s main part, after the opening courses.

dessert.definition: A dish served as the last course of a meal.

side-dish.definition: A prepared portion served with the main course adds contrasting flavor, texture, or nutritional value.

special.definition: A dish or meal given prominence in e.g. a restaurant.

bill.definition: A statement showing how much a customer must pay for their meal.
bill.exampleUsage: The bill was used during the activity.

check.definition: The bill for a restaurant meal, especially in American English.

tip.definition: Extra money given to staff for their service.

receipt.definition: A written or digital record showing that a payment was made.

reservation.definition: The act of reserving (a place or passage) or engaging the services of (a person or group).

order-pad.definition: A small pad or digital device used by restaurant staff to record customer orders.
order-pad.exampleUsage: The server wrote the food order on the order pad.

oven.definition: An enclosed heated compartment used to roast or bake meals.

stove.definition: A cooking appliance with heated burners on its top surface.

grill.definition: A metal surface used for cooking over a fire.

fryer.definition: A cooking appliance that cooks food in hot oil.

pot.definition: A deep round cooking vessel with handles, used for boiling or simmering.

pan.definition: A shallow round cooking vessel with a long handle.

cutting-board.definition: A flat protective surface used when chopping ingredients.

ladle.definition: A long-handled tool with a deep rounded end for serving soup.
ladle.exampleUsage: The ladle was used during the activity.

spatula.definition: A flat handheld tool used to lift, turn, or spread ingredients.
spatula.exampleUsage: The spatula was used during the activity.

whisk.definition: A wire kitchen tool used to beat ingredients and add air.
whisk.exampleUsage: The whisk was used during the activity.

mixer.definition: A kitchen machine that mixes or beats ingredients.

refrigerator.definition: A tall electric appliance that keeps fresh groceries cold.

freezer.definition: A very cold appliance that keeps groceries frozen for long storage.

sink.definition: A basin with running water and a drain used for washing dishes or hands.

soup.definition: A liquid dish made by cooking ingredients in water or stock.

salad.definition: Food mixtures either arranged on a plate or tossed and served with a moist dressing.

steak.definition: A slice of meat cut from the fleshy part of an animal or large fish.
steak.exampleUsage: The steak was identified during the lesson.

pasta.definition: A dough-based food shaped into noodles, tubes, or other forms.

pizza.definition: Italian open pie made of thin bread dough spread with a spiced mixture of e.g. tomato sauce and cheese.

sandwich.definition: Two (or more) slices of bread with a filling between them.

burger.definition: A sandwich consisting of a fried cake of minced beef served on a bun, often with other ingredients.

sushi.definition: A Japanese dish made with seasoned rice and toppings or fillings such as fish or vegetables.
sushi.exampleUsage: The sushi was identified during the lesson.

rice.definition: Small pale grains that become soft when boiled.

bread.definition: A baked staple made from dough, commonly sliced for sandwiches.

sauce.definition: Flavorful relish or dressing or topping served as an accompaniment to food.

dressing.definition: A sauce added to a salad.

garnish.definition: Something (such as parsley) added to a dish for flavor or decoration.

seasoning.definition: Salt, herbs, spices, or other ingredients added to give food flavor.
